statement: A video shows Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., playing a phone conversation between Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and Hunter Biden.
evidence: Is there a scandal involving Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., and President Joe Biden’s son Hunter? No, but an April 13 Facebook post claimed that a phone call between them suggests otherwise. "’YOU S.L£PT WITH HUNTER!’ - Sen John Kennedy PLAYS New Phone Conversation Between AOC & Potus Son | BREAKING NEWS," the post’s read. The post was flagged as part of Facebook’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. (Read more about our .) The video stitched two clips featuring Sen. John Kennedy, R-La. The first clip comes from a March 28 . In the clip, Kennedy questioned Department of Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas about issues at the border. Kennedy mentioned neither Ocasio-Cortez nor Biden. The second clip shows Kennedy speaking on the Senate floor . He spoke about the collapse of the Silicon Valley Bank, among other topics. Again, he made no mention of Ocasio-Cortez or Hunter Biden, much less played a phone conversation between them. We searched news archives and Google and found no reporting that reveals audio of a call between Ocasio-Cortez and Hunter Biden, nor did we find any legitimate reporting that Kennedy claimed to have such a recording. Fact-checkers at and have rated similar claims false. We rate this claim Pants on Fire!

statement: The U.S. Department of Defense awarded a contract for COVID-19 research in Ukraine months before the virus was known.
evidence: False claims about the COVID-19 pandemic being a government-invented scheme keep coming. This time, a video shared on shows Clayton Morris, a real estate investor and former TV news anchor, claiming that the U.S. Defense Department awarded Ukraine a contract for COVID-19 research months before the virus was discovered. "Why does United States government data show that the U.S. Department of Defense awarded a contract on the 12th of November 2019 to Labyrinth Gold Health Incorporated for COVID-19 research, at least one month before the alleged emergence of the novel Coronavirus, and three months before it was officially dubbed COVID 19?" Morris says. The video appears to come from of Morris’ YouTube show, "Redacted News." He goes on to claim that the contract was for research to be conducted in Ukraine and by the "The Exposé," a United Kingdom-focused website that has published COVID-19 misinformation. But this is wrong. TikTok identified the video as part of its efforts to counter inauthentic, misleading or false content. ( about PolitiFact’s partnership with TikTok.) The government contract was awarded in November 2019, but it wasn’t designated for COVID-19 research then. It was modified later, after the virus emerged. A search of USAspending.org, an open data source for federal spending information, shows that was awarded by the department’s to U.S. engineering company Black & Veatch. A went to international expert health organization Labyrinth Global Health on Nov. 12, 2019. The $369,511 description read, "SME (subject matter expert) MANUSCRIPT DOCUMENTATION AND COVID-19 RESEARCH." The first COVID-19 cases in the world were reported the following month, in December 2019, and the disease wasn’t But our reporting found that the contract’s description about "COVID-19 research" was added several months later — well after the virus started spreading worldwide. A Defense Threat Reduction Agency spokesperson confirmed that the organization didn’t award any contracts in 2019 for COVID-19 research and, instead, last modified a task order to an existing contract on June 10, 2020, to help Ukraine respond to the pandemic. Nov. 12, 2019, is when the initial contract (known formally as the "master servicing agreement") was entered into the system, agency spokesperson Andrea Chaney said in an email. The information on USASpending.gov shows agreement data that the Defense Department can modify over time in contracts to better address emerging issues. "Contractors frequently sign additional sub-awards through task orders. These task orders, too, can be modified or amended," Chaney said. "The date of each modification is not reflected on the USASpending.gov page, which stays as the date the original (master servicing agreement) was entered into the system, but the project description title is updated to reflect the latest changes in the task order." Chaney said the Defense Threat Reduction Agency contracted with Black & Veatch to continue supporting Ukraine’s "peaceful and safe biological detection and diagnostic capabilities" and to "reduce biological threats," whether naturally occurring, accidental or intentional. The company signed the agreement with the agency Oct. 2, 2019, for non-COVID training support, which was submitted in November 2019. The agency said the contract was modified after the pandemic began, in both April and June 2020, to provide additional COVID-19 pandemic-related support to Ukraine. "The task order directed the servicing contractor to provide high-level subject matter expert mentorship support on COVID-19 Laboratory Diagnosis, Biological Safety and Laboratory Emergency Response in Ukraine," Chaney wrote. The Defense Department did not pay for COVID-19 research in Ukraine before the virus emerged. We rate this claim False.

statement: Video shows Kenya’s president saying he will “get rid of U.S. dollar.”
evidence: A recent Instagram post claims that Kenyan President William Ruto said he will get rid of the U.S. dollar, a currency used in the country to buy imported goods. But that’s wrong, and takes his comments out of context. "For the people who work numbers, I am giving you free advice, that those of you who are holding dollars you shortly might go into losses. You better, you better do what you must do because this market is going to be different in a couple of weeks," Ruto says in a video clip in the March 27 . Text appearing over the video says: "Kenyan President to get rid of U.S. dollar." This post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. (Read more about our , which owns Facebook and Instagram.) On March 22, rather than saying that he was getting rid of the U.S. dollar, that the dollar will become more available in coming weeks. His remarks came after a dollar shortage in Kenya that caused fuel and oil importers to claim they were hobbled because they couldn’t access the currency. Imports such as medicine and food were also affected, German news outlet Deutsche Welle . Ruto said, "Dollar availability in the next couple of weeks is going to be very different because our fuel companies will now be paying for fuel in Kenya shillings. They do not have to look for dollars every month because we have done what we must do as government to ensure we ease the burden on people who want to realize their returns in dollars." So, Ruto wasn’t saying that dollars would become worthless because he was getting rid of them. He was saying that the surge in demand for dollars would wane because of the , freeing more U.S. dollars for circulation. We rate this post False.

statement: “Congress, White House, IRS, Feds, Federal Reserve are shut down.”
evidence: A recent Instagram post paints an apocalyptic picture in which central banks and U.S. corporations are all shuttering because they’re bankrupt, while some of the country's best known institutions have already done so. "Congress, White House, IRS, Feds, Rederal Reserve are shut down," the April 13 says, misspelling the Federal Reserve. Accompanying the claims is a photo of a pile of gold with this caption: "With 650 flights, 60,000 tons of gold has been returned to THE PEOPLE EARTH!! (that’s a drop in the bucket)!!! From the Vatican flew to America." This post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. (Read more about our , which owns Facebook and Instagram.) Congress, the White House, the Internal Revenue Service, the FBI and the Federal Reserve shutting down would constitute a huge news event, yet no such media reports exist. Both the U.S. House and U.S. Senate were in session April 13 — there’s — and both adjourned with plans to reconvene April 17. When we called the FBI’s national press office April 14, someone answered. Tax Day is looming (April 18, if you haven’t filed yet), and the IRS has been tweeting away about and . And although President Joe Biden is overseas, his press secretary continues to hold there and perform official duties. Plus, that photo of gold and claims that it came from the Vatican have been circulating for a while. In 2021, Agence France-Presse a claim that those and other gold bars had been seized in Vatican City, but there’s no evidence to support that claim, either. This particular photo was online as early as October 2016, in a Croatian news report about how the wealthy don’t trust banks with their gold. We rate claims that these government institutions have shut down Pants on Fire!

statement: “Fewer people get hurt playing rugby” than American football.
evidence: In a speech before the Irish parliament, President Joe Biden praised a sport more popular in Ireland than in the United States: rugby. Biden told the assembled lawmakers that he keeps an autographed rugby ball used in a 2021 game in which Ireland’s team defeated New Zealand’s fabled All Blacks. He said it was given to him by "one of Ireland’s greatest rugby stars, Rob Kearney," during a St. Patrick’s Day visit in 2022. Biden said he played a bit of rugby as a younger man, along with "American football and a few other sports." He said that, in retrospect, rugby might be a safer game. "I’d rather have my children playing rugby now, for health reasons, than I would have them playing football," Biden said. "Fewer people get hurt playing rugby. And you have no equipment. You have 280-pound guys like we do, and you just don’t hit each other in the head very often." Is Biden correct that rugby is a safer game than American football? Actually, most of the academic research suggests the opposite. "While the risk of injury in collision sports is substantial, rugby tends to have more injuries overall and more concussions than American football," said Thomas Buckley, associate professor in the department of kinesiology and applied physiology at the University of Delaware. In addition, he said, "players in both sports tend to have higher rates of neurodegenerative diseases such as mild cognitive impairment and dementia." First, a caveat: Comparing research on the two sports can be challenging because different metrics are used. For instance, some papers we found used overall injury rates, while others looked exclusively at concussions. Some studies looked at emergency room admissions while others compared longer-term health conditions. Some looked at school-age players while others studied professionals. And not all studies equalized their research to account for practice time and time spent off the field during games, which can alter the comparison of the two sports. It’s also worth noting for Americans unfamiliar with the sport that while American football players wear helmets and extensive padding, rugby uniforms involve far less protective padding and do not include a helmet. The White House did not provide supporting evidence for Biden’s statement, but we found our own. President Joe Biden addresses members of the Irish parliament on April 13, 2023. (New York Times via AP) Meta-analyses One type of study we came up with is called a meta-analysis, which looks at a wide range of existing studies and tries to draw broader conclusions about their collective findings. Perhaps the leading meta-analysis, in the journal Sports Medicine in 2021, looked at 83 studies. It found that rugby had the highest concussion rate of any sport, or about three times higher than the second-place sport, American football. The third- and fourth-place finishers were ice hockey and wrestling. Rugby was the only one of the sports studied that the authors labeled "high risk" based on these numbers. Meanwhile, a 2015 in the British Journal of Sports Medicine looked at 13 articles that addressed sports concussion rates. It found that rugby placed first, with a rate more than three times higher than ice hockey and eight times higher than American football. In a less formal analysis of the academic literature published in the journal Injuries and Sports Medicine in 2013, the authors that rugby "carries a significantly higher relative risk of injury than American football." Direct-comparison studies Direct-comparison studies are the closest thing to an apples-to-apples comparison. One , published in 2016 in the American Journal of Sports Medicine, looked at NCAA Division I injuries over three seasons for both sports. The authors found that the overall injury rate was about three times higher in rugby than in American football, and that a subset of this, the concussion rate, was about 2.5 times higher in rugby than in football. The authors deemed these differences to represent a "substantially higher" risk for rugby. Another researcher with experience in the field wrote a letter to the editor that critiqued these conclusions. Hamish Kerr, now a professor of medicine and pediatrics at Albany Medical Center who has worked as a physician for both USA Rugby and World Rugby, that the conclusion would flip if the methodology had taken into account that rugby players spend much more time on the field and engaging in athletic activity than football players do. This means that, adjusted for time played, rugby players’ injury rates would be lower. A paper on collegiate play in both sports in the British Journal of Sports Medicine by Kerr and several co-authors in 2008 supported that interpretation. Meanwhile, another , published in the journal Craniomaxillofacial Trauma & Reconstruction in 2022, looked at data from a 20-year injury database and found that "there was no difference in the rate of hospital admission when comparing football and rugby." However, this database would not capture injuries that didn’t rise to the level of a hospital admission. Finally, a study in the journal Sport Sciences for Health in 2022, looked at questionnaire responses from more than 2,000 Canadian high school students who had taken part in "collision-based sports," which included rugby, football, lacrosse and ice hockey. Here, the findings were somewhat mixed, though they still undercut Biden’s assertion that rugby was clearly a safer option than football. In overall injuries, rugby scored lower than the three other sports studied; ice hockey was highest, with an injury rate 2.6 times higher than rugby, while football and lacrosse were in the middle. It found the concussion data for rugby to be worrisome. Half of all injuries in rugby were concussions, more than twice the percentage in football, and the rate of concussions in rugby was slightly higher in rugby than in football. A focus on concussions Other research, while not directly comparing rugby and football, demonstrated concerns about the long-term effect of concussions among rugby players. For , American football has been with the of concussions on long-term neurological , including the risk of chronic traumatic encephalopathy, also known as CTE. But rugby is also grappling with these concerns. A 2022 in the Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery and Psychiatry looked at 32 former rugby players and a control group of 381 nonrugby players over roughly three decades. While the mortality rate was slightly lower for the rugby players through age 70, the players were more than twice as likely as control group members to be diagnosed with neurodegenerative diseases. Academic papers have found disproportionate evidence of CTE in both and players. As of this month, some 360 rugby players in the United Kingdom have joined a against their sports leagues for not taking sufficient precautions against concussions. Willie Stewart, a neuropathologist at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital in Glasgow, Scotland, who co-authored the paper in the Journal of Neurology, Neurosurgery and Psychiatry, said that such studies should be taken as persuasive evidence of rugby’s risks. "Brains are the main issue we should worry about," Stewart said. "Knees and hips we can live with when damaged, or replace them. Brains we get a one-time supply of, and when damaged, it's irreparable and irreplaceable."

statement: “In America our own (central bank digital currency) system is going to be launching July 1. It’s called the FedNow payment system.”
evidence: In recent months, social media has been rife with baseless fears that the U.S. government is seeking to replace paper money with a central bank digital currency to control its citizens. A new claim shared on TikTok put a name and timetable to the plan’s supposed implementation. But it falsely conflates a potential central bank digital currency that is only under consideration and has no timetable for implementation with a Federal Reserve System instant payment system that has an upcoming launch date. "In America our own (central bank digital currency) system is going to be launching July 1. It’s called the FedNow payment system," said the speaker in a on TikTok. The speaker also says its purpose is for the government to track how Americans spend their money. TikTok identified this video as part of its efforts to counter inauthentic, misleading or false content. ( about PolitiFact's partnership with TikTok.) We’ve debunked such before, which have been among conservatives, even government leaders like . A central bank digital currency system is not launching in July. The Federal Reserve System is studying the benefits and drawbacks of such a system but has not proposed implementing it. The FedNow Service is a separate initiative from the Federal Reserve System — the country’s central bank — and it’s . It will let financial institutions provide instant payment services to customers, . FedNow will replace existing payment systems , a nationwide network the Federal Reserve helps operate. Banks use the automated clearinghouse to send electronic credit and debit transfers for things such as payroll, tax refunds and mortgages. FedNow will be similar to private systems like Zelle or Venmo, and its use by banks would be optional. It is expected to . Separately, the Federal Reserve has been studying the possibility of creating a central bank digital currency, according to news . It issued a in January 2022 that laid out potential benefits and risks of such a system. President Joe Biden in March 2022 signed an directing the U.S. government to evaluate the feasibility of a potential central bank digital currency. But there are no plans in place to implement it, and such a system may never happen. Doing so would require congressional action, Fed Chair Jerome Powell March 8 to the House Financial Services Committee. Most Americans already keep their money in mostly digital form, such as payment apps and banks, the Federal Reserve’s . The difference is that a central bank digital currency would be a liability of the Federal Reserve rather than commercial banks. The Federal Reserve said central bank digital currency, if implemented, would not replace paper currency and that of consumers is critical. Experts have that current U.S. laws do not allow the kind of surveillance and control that the video claims the government would possess with a central digital bank currency system. We rate the claim that, "In America our own (central bank digital currency) system is going to be launching July 1. It’s called the FedNow payment system," False.

statement: “La NASA advierte que el sol podría dejar de brillar y causar una catástrofe”.
tags: Climate Change; Natural Disasters; PolitiFact en Español
evidence: El mundo ha pasado por muchas catástrofes climáticas afectando la vida de muchas personas, lo cual ha hecho que científicos investiguen cuáles son los factores que crean estos escenarios. Un circulando en Facebook alega que "la NASA advierte que el sol podría dejar de brillar y causar una catástrofe". El video del 6 de abril, el cual incluye un segmento de un noticiero, dice que la NASA alertó de que el sol está apunto de entrar en una fase que genera una baja drástica de temperaturas, lo que podría desatar catástrofes a nivel global y hambruna. La publicación fue marcada como parte del esfuerzo de Meta para combatir las noticias falsas y la desinformación en su plataforma. ( dueño de Facebook e Instagram). PolitiFact contactó a la NASA para verificar la veracidad del video. "El video no tiene alegaciones válidas,", dijo Denise Hill, una vocera de la NASA. Hill dijo que el sol tiene ciclos y que cada nuevo ciclo solar viene aproximadamente cada 11 años. En el curso de cada ciclo, el sol transiciona de estar relativamente calmado a estar activo y tormentoso, y después callado de nuevo. En su punto más alto, conocido como el máximo solar, los polos magnéticos del sol se voltean. El periodo silencioso es conocido como el mínimo solar y el último mínimo solar ocurrió en diciembre del 2019. Durante el máximo solar, cambios en el magnetismo del sol produce un número más grande de manchas solares, más energía y causa erupciones solares de partículas. Este es el proceso normal del sol, dijo Hill. "Entender el comportamiento del sol es importante porque los estallidos del sol, incluidas las erupciones conocidas como erupciones solares y eyecciones de masa coronal, pueden perturbar satélites y las señales de comunicación que viajan alrededor de la tierra", dijo Hill. "Los científicos estudian el ciclo solar para que puedan predecir y prepararse mejor para la actividad solar". Los cambios en pocos periodos de tiempo en solar no son lo suficientemente fuertes para tener influencia a largo plazo en el clima de la tierra. NASA describe la irradiación solar "como la salida de la energía solar del todo el del sol, medido en la tierra". "Los científicos están de acuerdo en que el ciclo solar y sus cambios asociados a corto plazo en la irradiación, no pueden ser la fuerza principal que impulsa los cambios en el clima de la tierra que estamos viendo actualmente", dice la en una página web. Investigadores de la han dicho que eventualmente el combustible del sol, que es el hidrógeno, se va a acabar, pero esto va a pasar en 5 mil millones de años. Otros astrónomos estiman que al sol le quedan por lo menos 7 mil millones de años antes de que muera. La longevidad del sol de la tierra es de 10 mil millones de años y ya ha vivido 4.5 mil millones de años, . Nuestra calificación Un video en Facebook alega que, "la NASA advierte que el sol podría dejar de brillar y causar una catástrofe". El sol si podría dejar de brillar, pero el video da la impresión incorrecta de que esto puede pasar pronto. Se espera que el sol dure miles de millones de años más. Los científicos dicen que, los ciclos del sol son normales y sus cambios pequeños no tiene influencia a largo plazo en el clima de la tierra. Los cambios de irradiación solar más largos son cambios que ocurren en décadas y estos solo pueden tener un impacto climático junto con otros factores naturales e influencias humanas. La publicación contiene un elemento de verdad pero ignora hechos críticos que darían una impresión diferente. La calificamos como Mayormente Falsa.

statement: The person purporting to be Tiffany Dover is an impostor.
evidence: NBC News reporter Brandy Zadrozny recently published a report that should have put to rest unfounded claims that Tiffany Dover, a nurse who fainted after getting her first COVID-19 vaccine dose in December 2020 in Tennessee, had died. "Tiffany Dover is alive," Zadrozny . "Sitting across from Tiffany at her kitchen table, this is obvious. She breathes in and out. She gestures with her hands. She laughs generously." Dover withdrew from the public eye after fainting on camera. She stopped posting on her social media accounts and gave no interviews. She told Zadrozny that the hospital directed her not to post online or take outside calls. But that silence seemed to fuel the flames of a conspiracy theory that the COVID-19 vaccine had killed her. Now that Dover is newly back online, and in the news, some people are still claiming that she’s dead and that the person who appears in her social media posts isn’t her but a dupe. "They think we are so stupid," reads one Instagram , sharing a TikTok Dover made and shared on Instagram on April 10. "Tiffany Dover has resurrected." Comments on the post range from "this woman doesn’t look like her at all" to "Lol after people have been looking for her for years, she’s coming out of the blue?! Please." This post was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. (Read more about our , which owns Facebook and Instagram.) Dover has lightened her hair since she fainted in 2020. It’s now blond rather than dark brown. But a trip to the salon does not amount to a conspiracy theory. Her bright blue eyes are the same color as they were in 2020. And back then, the hospital where she was employed repeatedly responded to rumors of her death and later to PolitiFact that she was, indeed, alive. "Hey guys, I know it’s been a really long time and I don’t even know where to begin, but I guess I could start with: I’m alive," Dover says in the TikTok video that’s drawing claims that she’s not who she says she is. Those claims are baseless. We rate them Pants on Fire!

statement: HIV is not contagious.
evidence: A Facebook post included a video of a doctor injecting himself with what he said was blood infected with . HIV is the virus that cause AIDS, a potentially fatal that weakens the immune system. "He wanted to prove that the HIV virus was not contagious," text imposed over the excerpts read. "He never tested positive." The post itself said: "The greatest lie ever told?" The was flagged as part of Meta’s efforts to combat false news and misinformation on its News Feed. (Read more about our with Meta, which owns Facebook and Instagram.) HIV is contagious. In the U.S., an estimated 1.2 million people had HIV at the end of 2019, to the most recent federal data. HIV is passed by bodily fluids, through unprotected sex and sharing of drug injection equipment such as needles. The late Dr. Robert Willner, a Florida physician who believed that HIV does not cause AIDS, did the injection demonstration in 1994 during an alternative medicine meeting in Greensboro, North Carolina, The Washington Post at the time. The demonstration is shown in . Willner stuck a hypodermic needle into a finger of a man who Willner said was HIV-positive, then stuck the needle into his own finger. During the demonstration, Willner called Dr. Anthony Fauci and other top federal health officials criminals. Fauci was director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases until December 2022. He played key roles in the public health response to AIDS and the COVID-19 pandemic. HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) spreads through bodily fluids, including semen, pre-ejaculatory fluid, rectal fluids, vaginal fluids and breast milk. The majority of transmission cases occur during unprotected sex or from needles or other drug injection equipment. HIV and destroys white blood cells in the blood. These cells are part of the immune system and normally defend the human body against disease and infection. AIDS (acquired immune deficiency syndrome) is the severe stage of HIV infection. Most people with HIV do not get AIDS, to the federal health website HIV.gov. AIDS was as a new disease in 1981 when increasing numbers of young, gay men succumbed to unusual infections and rare malignancies. More than U.S. residents have died from HIV-related illness. HIV-related mortality rates steadily through the 1980s and peaked in 1995. With improved treatments, the death rate has in half since 2009, according to the Kaiser Family Foundation. Without HIV treatment, people with AIDS typically survive about three years, to the federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The claim that HIV is not contagious is false and ridiculous. We rate it Pants on Fire!

statement: "Latino, inmigrante, recién llegado … Si eres inmigrante en Estados Unidos y llevas más de tres meses ahí, podrías calificar para obtener cupones de comida”.

evidence: Muchos recién llegados a los Estados Unidos tienen varios trámites que hacer, incluyendo gestiones administrativas de inmigración, buscar empleo y asegurar que hay algo para comer en la mesa cada día. El video no especifica de qué programa de cupones está hablando. Sin embargo, existe un programa federal que permite a estadounidenses y ciertos inmigrantes de bajos ingresos acceder a fondos para comprar comida nutritiva.
